sources.title: Bounds on the Expansion Properties of Tanner Graphs
sources.comparison: The bit-oriented bound is s(H) >= n(2γ−η)/(γk−η), η=σ₂², with binary regular incidence. It concerns the same graph stopping distance, but does not construct QC-GHP matrices meeting η<γ/2. The parity-oriented bound and multi-eigenvector expansion analysis supply older alternatives to the weak mixing step.

sources.title: Minimum Distance Bounds by Graph Analysis
sources.inspected_version: Inspected manuscript dated July 26, 2000; 2001 journal version not inspected
sources.comparison: Theorems assume a connected regular bipartite graph, with constant bit and check degrees. Theorem 3.1 gives n(2γ−η)/(γk−η) for classical distance. Its at-least-two-active-bits proof is the ancestor of Zhu–Chugg’s explicit stopping-distance extension. This is not the same γ/2 test, nor a QC-GHP parameter theorem. The manuscript reports an earlier 1982 submission; this is not treated as an inspected 1982 publication.

sources.title: Degenerate Quantum LDPC Codes With Good Finite Length Performance
sources.comparison: Original construction source. Quantum logical distance excludes stabilizers; graph stopping distance does not. The conclusion explicitly notes special-case lower bounds for C(A,1+x) in footnote 19. Those results neither imply the source’s raw singular-value condition nor answer its stopping-bound question.

sources.title: Quantum Tanner codes
sources.comparison: Ramanujan expansion is imposed on constituent Cayley graphs, together with local-code distance, dual-tensor robustness, puncturing resistance and total no-conjugacy. It is not a statement that the expanded CSS parity-check matrix has σ₂²<γ/2. It does not furnish parameters for Proposition 5.1. Efficient decoding is a historical question in this 2022 version; current resolution is deliberately unassessed in this screen.
